text:
Stock Market Rally Ramps Up On Apple, Boeing, Facebook, Fed; Amazon, Microsoft, Nvidia Weak By 0 34
The current stock market rally powered higher, fueled by a earnings from Apple ( AAPL ), Boeing ( BA ) and Facebook ( FB ), even as Amazon.com ( AMZN ), Microsoft ( MSFT ), Nvidia ( NVDA ), DowDuPont ( DWDP ) were among earnings disappointments. A dovish Fed, strong jobs report and optimism over China trade talks also buoyed the stock market.
X Stock Market Rally Powers Higher
The major averages pushed above a recent mini-consolidation to their best levels since early December. Earnings reports were generally positive, with Apple stock, Facebook stock and Boeing stock surged on results. A dovish Fed and strong jobs and manufacturing data also provided support. Several more top stocks broke out, bolstering the current stock market rally. Apple Buoyed By Services Growth
Despite soft iPhone sales in the holiday Q1, Apple ( AAPL ) earned $4.18 a share, up 7% year over year, on sales of $84.3 billion, down 5%,. Analysts expected earnings of $4.17 a share on sales of $84 billion. Apple's iPhone revenue declined 15% in the quarter, while sales from all other products and services grew 19%. Apple's hardware, including iPhone, iPad, Mac and other devices, had a gross margin of 34.3%. Its services had a gross margin of 62.8%, which topped analyst estimates for 60%. For the current quarter, Apple expects revenue of $55 billion to $59 billion, or $57 billion at the midpoint. Wall Street had been modeling $59 billion. But Apple stock soared nearly 6% for the week. Fed Tame, Jobs Report Strong
Wall Street cheered Friday's unexpectedly strong jobs and manufacturing data, thanks to the Fed. After the Fed signaled that rate hikes are off the table at least until midyear, strong data only provide cause for celebration — not fear that they'll provoke more monetary tightening. Slowing global growth, financial market angst, a waning of federal stimulus have raised concern about the outlook, but the new data are encouraging.
The economy added 304,000 jobs. Downward revisions to early gains left the 3-month average at a robust 241,000. The unemployment rate ticked up to 4.0%, partly due to the government shutdown. Wage growth was a bit soft, with a 0.1% monthly gain, but the 3.2% annual rate was just off a nine-year high.
The Institute for Supply Management's manufacturing survey index jumped 2.3 points in January to 56.6. That's below the lofty levels that prevailed through November of last year, but way above the 50 neutral level. The new orders index surged 6.9 points to 58.2, though export orders slipped closer to neutral. Facebook Earnings, Users Strong
Facebook stock soared 11% as a strong earnings report showed advertisers and users sticking with the social media giant despite data privacy scandals. Facebook ( FB ) ended the quarter with 1.52 billion daily active users, up 9% from the year-ago period. Average revenue per user soared, mostly from U.S. and Canada users. Amazon Stock Falls On Guidance
Amazon beat fourth-quarter earnings estimates easily, but it expects Q1 revenue growth of just 10%-18%, which would be the slowest pace in more than three years. The e-commerce giant also said it will step up spending on investments. Amazon stock fell 5.4% Friday. Boeing Soars On Strong Earnings, Guidance
Boeing ( BA ) earnings per share climbed 14% to $5.48 a share while revenue rose 11.7% to $28.34 billion. Both beat analyst views. Commercial aircraft revenue climbed 12% to $17.3 billion. Defense revenue grew 16% to $6.11 billion. Management expects slow Q1 delivery activity but sees 2019 deliveries of 895-905, up 11.7% at the midpoint vs. 2018 deliveries of 806. Boeing sees full-year EPS of $19.90-$20.10, well above consensus for $19.24. Boeing stock rose more than 6%, breaking out, nearly hitting a record high. Aerospace Suppliers Strong
TransDigm ( TDG ), which supplies parts for Boeing, Airbus ( EADSY ), Lockheed Martin ( LMT ) and more, reported a fourth straight quarter of accelerating revenue growth. Shares soared, breaking out past a buy point. Meanwhile, Woodward ( WWD ), whose aerospace segment makes controls systems, also raced past buy zone after scored an earnings beat. It had been consolidating for almost a year. Spirit AeroSystems ( SPR ) topped EPS views but missed on sales. Revenue guidance was strong. Microsoft Outlook Disappoints
Microsoft ( MSFT ) sees current-quarter sales rising 11% to $29.75 billion. Wall Street predicted $29.9 billion. Microsoft reported adjusted Q2 earnings of $1.10 a share, up 15%, on sales of $32.5 billion, up 12%, in the December quarter. Analysts expected it to earn $1.09 a share on sales of $32.5 billion. Microsoft was hurt by weakness in PC-linked businesses like Windows and consumer Office software. Enterprise cloud businesses like Azure helped offset that. Shares fell 4%. Nvidia Warns On Revenue
Graphics-chip maker Nvidia ( NVDA ) sees revenue of $2.2 billion in Q4 ended Jan. 27, down from its prior target of $2.7 billion, citing weakness in its gaming and data center systems. Advanced Micro Devices ( AMD ) met EPS views, slightly missed on sales and lowered expectations for the current quarter. But after tumbling on Nvidia's warning, AMD soared 20% Wednesday. Mellanox Technologies ( MLNX ) beat estimates and also rallied on a report that Intel wants to buy it. GE Stock Skyrockets
General Electric ( GE ) earnings of 17 cents fell short by a penny, but revenue of $33.28 billion smashed expectations for $32.0 billion. Analysts said debt and cash-flow challenges appear to be easing. Gains in GE's “crown jewel” aviation unit appear to be offsetting further declines in its mainstay power business. GE stock made a massive post-earnings move, surging 12% Thursday for its best one-day move in nearly a decade. Earlier in the week, Caterpillar ( CAT ) badly missed Q4 EPS views, while DowDuPont ( DWDP ) plunged on weak sales and guidance. 3M ( MMM ) earnings topped estimates modestly, lifting its stock. On Friday, Honeywell narrowly beat Q4 views. Tesla Profit Misses, CFO Exits
Tesla ( TSLA ) reported fourth-quarter earnings that topped revenue estimates but fell short on the bottom line. The company also announced the departure of CFO Deepak Ahuja. His successor is Tesla finance executive Zach Kirkhorn. Tesla stock rose 5% for the week. Alibaba Earnings
The China e-commerce company beat on earnings but missed on revenue. Revenue from its cloud-computing business increased 84% from a year earlier to $962 million. Alibaba ( BABA ) stock rose 5.5%, hitting resistance at the 200-day line. ServiceNow Breaks Out
The enterprise software maker's adjusted fourth-quarter earnings rose 120% to 77 cents a share, topping estimates of 64 cents. Revenue rose 30% to $715.4 million, slightly missing views. ServiceNow ( NOW ) forecast 2019 subscription billings growth of 31% to 32%, in a range of $3.705 billion to $3.725 billion. That beat analyst estimates for $3.644 billion. ServiceNow blasted 16% to a record high. Mastercard, Visa Break Out, PayPal Slumps
Mastercard ( MA ) broke out on after the firm bested Q4 earnings views and issued upbeat revenue guidance. Credit card rival Visa ( V ) initially fell despite beating Q1 views, after warning on risks to consumer spending. But shares rallied Friday ot move above a buy point too. Finally, PayPal ( PYPL ) tumbled after the digital payments leader's revenue only met views, while revenue guidance was light. All three stocks are on the IBD 50. Lockheed, Defense Peers Guide Low For 2019
Lockheed Martin ( LMT ) met views for a 2% EPS gain to $4.39. Revenue was $14.41 billion, beating estimates. Aeronautics revenue rose 4% to $5.88 billion, led by the F-35. Lockheed sees full year EPS of $19.15-$19.45, with the midpoint below consensus of $19.40. General Dynamics ( GD ), Northrop Grumman ( NOC ) and Raytheon ( RTN ) all issued weaker than expected guidance for 2019. Drug Earnings
Dow Jones drug giants Pfizer ( PFE ) and Merck ( MRK ) topped quarterly views, along with Allergan ( AGN ) topped expectations. Merck's 2019 guidance was in line, but Pfizer's was weak. Allergan's sales outlook was light, though it guided earnings higher. Novartis ( NVS ) missed earnings and sales targets, but revenue guidance was in line. Biotech Earnings
Biogen ( BIIB ) topped Q4 views and issued solid guidance. It announced another test of its Alzheimer's treatment, aducanumab, but fell Wednesday after Roche and AC Immune scrapped a pair of studies for a rival drug. Amgen ( AMGN ) beat Q4 estimates, but 2019 guidance lagged. Celgene ( CELG ), which is being acquired by Bristol-Myers Squibb ( BMY ) had a beat-and-raise report. Medtech Earnings
Medtech firms Stryker ( SYK ), Abiomed ( ABMD ) and Baxter ( BAX ) all topped quarterly earnings expectations last week. Stryker also issued strong 2019 EPS guidance while Abiomed gave bullish revenue guidance. Edwards Lifesciences met EPS views and topped on sales, but 2019 EPS guidance was light. Health Insurers
Anthem stock surged past a buy point on the strength of a fourth-quarter earnings surprise. The health insurer also offered bullish guidance for 2019 and hit fast-forward on a strategic shift that will help in 2020 and beyond. But Cigna fell Friday on disappointing guidance and a new Trump administration rule aimed at prescription drug middlemen. The proposed rule would deny new Cigna acquisition Express Scripts and other PBMs, including CVS Health ( CVS ), from pocketing rebates. Exxon Earnings Jump As Permian Output Soars
Exxon Mobil ( XOM ) reported EPS jumped to $1.41, crushing estimates, but revenue fell short. Production in the Permian Basin jumped more than 90%. Capital spending dropped 13% to $7.84 billion. Chevron ( CVX ) posted EPS of $1.95, more than doubling from the year-ago-quarter. Revenue beat estimates. Production rose 12% to 3.08 million barrels of oil equivalent per day. Capital spending rose 6% to $5.76 billion. Chevron sees production growing 4%-7% in 2019. McDonald's Warns On Costs
Labor costs, commodity costs and depreciation related to a big remodeling drive will strain profits this year. But McDonald's ( MCD ) CEO said he was “not at all” concerned that some franchisees' efforts to band together into an advocacy group would disrupt business. Q4 results were mixed, as an array of value meals and discounts made for tough competition. Yum China ( YUMC ) topped earnings and same-store sales expectations, sending shares higher. Telecom Earnings
AT&T ( T ) and Verizon ( VZ ) fell short on Q4 revenue while the former also fell short on wireless postpaid subscribers and DirecTV customers. Verizon expects capital spending to rise 5% or more in 2019 as it expands 5G wireless broadband services. Sprint, which is seeking regulators' approval to merge with T-Mobile US ( TMUS ), topped revenue views and lost fewer customers than expected. News In Brief
UPS ( UPS ) earnings climbed 16% to $1.94 as revenue rose 5% to $19.85 billion. The delivery giant said transformation efforts are paying off and offsetting slower global growth.
After seven months without a permanent chief executive, Intel ( INTC ) selected Bob Swan, interim CEO and chief financial officer, to lead the company.
Illumina ( ILMN ) earnings of $1.32 per share ex items missed views while $867 million in sales beat.
Deckers Outdoor ( DECK ) soared 10.5% Friday after the maker of Ugg boots and other footwear reported blowout earnings and strong revenue.
